fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Circular Driveway; Walkway; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Circular Driveway; Detached Structure Complexity; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so responding units can pull through without backing out.
• Mark or label the detached structure on any posted site map so arriving crews know a second building is on the property.
• Post a site map near the driveway entrance showing the locations of the main residence, detached structure, and any utility shutoffs.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway to maintain clear sightlines and overhead clearance for responding vehicles.
• Create or maintain a pedestrian path connecting the main residence to the detached structure that is passable on foot at night.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing at the rear of the property unlocked and accessible for emergency crews.
• If rear access through the fencing requires a key or combination, provide that information to the local fire department.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Large Trees
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that overhang or touch the structure.
• Thin shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Remove grass and low ground cover that connects shrub patches to the base of the structure.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep the full width and height clear for emergency vehicles.
• Clear shrubs and tall grass from the edges of the driveway to maintain visibility and movement along the single access route.
• Separate shrub clusters from the base of large trees to reduce the chance that low burning material reaches the tree canopy.
